CARD_DOC_ID: 1GAG78Tv0-GMlThFGWkY1rXj24HBnY6-ENIb2nZUryR8


1. Scope


229AR supplies the no-threshold-loss quadratic-height receiver
  W_- = UV-eR,
with
  G_* = gcd(eR,UV) = gcd(eR,W_-),
  K_odd = sf_odd(W_-),
and
  2W_- = lambda S,
where
  lambda := U+V-R-e > 0,
  S      := e+U+V+R.


229AQ also uses the shifted positive linear pair
  L_- := e+U+V-R = lambda+2e,
  L_+ := R+U+V-e = lambda+2R,
for which
  L_- L_+ = 2(UV+eR).


This card proves that the odd raw content G_* itself, not only its squareclass, splits exactly into two coprime O(B)-height gcd packets in each of these two linear pairings. The two pairings are crossed matchings of four pairwise-coprime atomic linear-linear gcd buckets.


The result strengthens the low-height theorem interface while preserving the 229AR no-threshold-loss receiver and the 229AQ central divisor chart.


Notation:
  d0 := gcd(x,y).
Retain 229O:
  gcd(eR,d0)=1.
For an integer n, n_odd denotes its odd part; gcd_odd means the odd part of a gcd.


2. The common odd gcd of lambda and S is d0-square-supported


Set
  h_0 := gcd_odd(lambda,S).                       (229AS.1)


Let an odd prime power p^j divide h_0. Then p^j divides
  lambda+S = 2(U+V),
  S-lambda = 2(R+e).
Since p is odd,
  p^j | U+V,
  p^j | R+e.


Therefore
  p^j | U^2-V^2 = x^2-y^2,
and
  p^j | R^2-e^2 = x^2+y^2.
Hence
  p^j | 2x^2,
  p^j | 2y^2.
Again p is odd, so
  p^j | gcd(x^2,y^2)=d0^2.


Thus
  h_0 | d0^2.                                    (229AS.2)


Retain gcd(eR,d0)=1. Therefore
  gcd(eR,h_0)=1.                                 (229AS.3)


RESULT_229AS_CENTRAL_COMMON_GCD_DIVIDES_d0_SQUARED=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AS_CENTRAL_COMMON_GCD_COPRIME_TO_eR=PROVED_EXACT.


In particular the common odd factors of lambda and S are pure missing-face-scale nuisance. They do not carry any odd prime of G_*.


3. The shifted pair has the same nuisance firewall


Let
  h_1 := gcd_odd(L_-,L_+).                       (229AS.4)


If p^j is an odd prime power dividing h_1, then
  p^j | L_-+L_+ = 2(U+V),
  p^j | L_+-L_- = 2(R-e).
Thus
  p^j | U+V,
  p^j | R-e.


As above,
  p^j | x^2-y^2,
  p^j | x^2+y^2,
so
  p^j | d0^2.


Hence
  h_1 | d0^2,                                    (229AS.5)
and by 229O
  gcd(eR,h_1)=1.                                 (229AS.6)


RESULT_229AS_SHIFTED_COMMON_GCD_DIVIDES_d0_SQUARED=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AS_229AQ_gL_IS_d0_SQUARE_SUPPORTED_AND_GSTAR_FREE=PROVED_EXACT.


This sharpens the role of the 229AQ common odd divisor: it is not an uncontrolled moving part of the K_* support.


4. First exact raw-G odd matching: lambda versus S


Define
  Q_- := gcd_odd(eR,lambda),
  Q_+ := gcd_odd(eR,S).                           (229AS.7)


Any common odd divisor of Q_- and Q_+ divides both eR and h_0. By (229AS.3),
  gcd(Q_-,Q_+)=1.                                (229AS.8)


Using 229AR,
  lambda S = 2W_-,
  W_-=UV-eR,
and
  gcd(eR,W_-)
   =gcd(eR,UV)
   =G_*.


Therefore
  Q_- Q_+
   =gcd_odd(eR,lambda S)
   =gcd_odd(eR,W_-)
   =(G_*)_odd.                                   (229AS.9)


RESULT_229AS_CENTRAL_TWO_GCD_MATCHING_RAW_GODD=PROVED_EXACT.


Thus the complete odd raw content is exactly the product of two coprime gcd values, each involving eR and one O(B)-height positive linear form.


Height:
  0<lambda<R-e<B,
  R<S<4R<=4B.                                    (229AS.10)


5. Second exact raw-G odd matching: L_- versus L_+


Define
  P_- := gcd_odd(eR,L_-),
  P_+ := gcd_odd(eR,L_+).                         (229AS.11)


By (229AS.6),
  gcd(P_-,P_+)=1.                                (229AS.12)


Retain
  L_-L_+ = 2W_+,
  W_+ := UV+eR.
Also
  gcd(eR,W_+)
   =gcd(eR,UV)
   =G_*.


Hence
  P_-P_+
   =gcd_odd(eR,L_-L_+)
   =gcd_odd(eR,W_+)
   =(G_*)_odd.                                   (229AS.13)


RESULT_229AS_SHIFTED_TWO_GCD_MATCHING_RAW_GODD=PROVED_EXACT.


The packet heights are
  0<L_-<2B,
  R<L_+<3B.                                      (229AS.14)


Thus 229AS produces two distinct exact two-packet raw-G factorizations, both with linear-height packet values.


6. Four atomic linear-linear gcd buckets


Define
  A_- := gcd_odd(e,lambda),
  A_+ := gcd_odd(e,S),
  C_- := gcd_odd(R,lambda),
  C_+ := gcd_odd(R,S).                            (229AS.15)


We first split the central matching:
  Q_- = A_- C_-,
  Q_+ = A_+ C_+.                                 (229AS.16)


To justify the products, note that an odd prime dividing e,R and lambda would satisfy
  U+V ≡ 0 mod p,
  R ≡ e ≡ 0 mod p.
Then
  x^2-y^2 = U^2-V^2 ≡0 mod p,
  x^2+y^2 = R^2-e^2 ≡0 mod p,
so p divides x and y, contradicting the primitive physical condition gcd(e,x,y)=1.
The same argument works with S in place of lambda.


Hence the e- and R-parts of each Q packet are coprime and (229AS.16) is exact.


Now retain the exact physical contents
  gcd(e,U)=b,
  gcd(e,V)=a,
and gcd(a,b)=1.
Therefore
  gcd(e,UV)=ab.                                   (229AS.17)


Likewise the Pythagorean triples (U,y,R) and (V,x,R) have contents c12 and c21, so their pairwise gcds satisfy
  gcd(R,U)=c12,
  gcd(R,V)=c21.
Since gcd(c12,c21)=1,
  gcd(R,UV)=c12 c21.                              (229AS.18)


Using lambda S=2W_- and the same d0-square common-gcd firewall,
  A_-A_+
   =gcd_odd(e,W_-)
   =(ab)_odd,                                     (229AS.19)
and
  C_-C_+
   =gcd_odd(R,W_-)
   =(c12 c21)_odd.                                (229AS.20)


Since the four physical contents a,b,c12,c21 are pairwise coprime, and the central sign packets on each side are coprime, the four atomic buckets
  A_-, A_+, C_-, C_+
are pairwise coprime.


Consequently
  (G_*)_odd
   = A_- A_+ C_- C_+.                            (229AS.21)


RESULT_229AS_FOUR_ATOMIC_LINEAR_LINEAR_GCD_BUCKETS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AS_EDGE_RAW_CONTENT_SPLIT_BY_CENTRAL_SIGN=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AS_SPACE_RAW_CONTENT_SPLIT_BY_CENTRAL_SIGN=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AS_FOUR_ATOMIC_BUCKETS_PAIRWISE_COPRIME=PROVED_EXACT.


Each atomic bucket is a gcd of two O(B)-height linear integer coordinates/forms.


7. The second matching is the crossed pairing of the same four atoms


Use
  L_- = lambda+2e,
  L_+ = lambda+2R,
  S-L_+ = 2e,
  S-L_- = 2R.


Therefore
  gcd_odd(e,L_-)=A_-,
  gcd_odd(e,L_+)=A_+,
  gcd_odd(R,L_-)=C_+,
  gcd_odd(R,L_+)=C_-.                             (229AS.22)


Hence the shifted matching is exactly
  P_- = A_- C_+,
  P_+ = A_+ C_-.                                 (229AS.23)


Together with the central matching
  Q_- = A_- C_-,
  Q_+ = A_+ C_+,                                 (229AS.24)
this is a crossed 2x2 matching of the same four pairwise-coprime raw-content atoms.


RESULT_229AS_CROSSED_TWO_MATCHING_IDENTITY=PROVED_EXACT.


This is not the 229AN event-equivalent reparameterization: the two matchings are genuinely different pairings. However, every possible choice of one Q packet and one P packet shares exactly one atomic bucket:

  Q_- with P_+ shares C_-,
  Q_+ with P_- shares C_+,
  Q_+ with P_+ shares A_+.


Therefore the two matching incidences must not be multiplied as independent local densities.


RESULT_229AS_CROSSED_MATCHING_DEPENDENCE_FIREWALL=PROVED_EXACT.


8. Simultaneous half-threshold statement


Let
  K_odd := sf_odd(G_*).


By the coprime exact products,
  K_odd
   =sf(Q_-) sf(Q_+)
   =sf(P_-) sf(P_+).                              (229AS.25)


If

then
  K_odd>T/2.
Therefore simultaneously:
- at least one of Q_-,Q_+ has squarefree kernel > (T/2)^(1/2);
- at least one of P_-,P_+ has squarefree kernel > (T/2)^(1/2).


At the current threshold
  T=B^(1/3-delta),
the common low-height packet threshold is
  2^(-1/2) B^(1/6-delta/2).                     (229AS.26)


RESULT_229AS_SIMULTANEOUS_CROSSED_HALF_THRESHOLD=PROVED_EXACT.


This matches the exponent of the 229AQ two-packet receiver but upgrades the packet objects to exact raw-content gcds:
  gcd_odd(eR, positive O(B)-height linear form).


No counting gain follows merely from having both crossed matchings, because of the atomic shared-factor dependence in Section 7.


9. Current theorem interface after 229AS

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AR — macro-Pythagorean content collapse and no-threshold-loss bilinear gap receiver


STATUS: POST_229AQ_MACRO_PYTHAGOREAN_COLLAPSE_COMPLETE / PROVED_eR_xy_UV_IS_SINGLE_PHYSICAL_PYTHAGOREAN_TRIPLE / PROVED_GSTAR_EQUALS_ITS_EXACT_CONTENT_AND_GCD_eR_UV / PROVED_BILINEAR_SUM_DIFFERENCE_ARE_CONTENT_TIMES_COPRIME_SQUARES_UP_TO_ONE_2 / PROVED_NO_THRESHOLD_LOSS_SINGLE_SCALAR_KSTAR_RECEIVER / PROVED_229AQ_TWO_PRODUCTS_CARRY_RAW_GSTAR_TIMES_SQUARE / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AQ EXACT MACRO-PYTHAGOREAN CONTENT / SINGLE-SCALAR SQUAREFREE RECEIVER / EUCLID-ROOT COMPRESSION / NO-THRESHOLD-LOSS THEOREM INTERFACE / METHOD FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AQ
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1jzJ7yV0SoCU9sxBCN4d2bDj5Bmf3c8MchdQCP-cb4nc


1. Scope


229AQ gave an exact four-short-gap squarefree-kernel collapse, then a two-linear O(B)-height packetization
  d_tw=sf(L_- L_+),
  K_odd=sf_odd(L_- L_+),
with
  L_-=e+U+V-R,
  L_+=R+U+V-e,
and a packet threshold T^(1/2).


There is a stronger exact whole-support identity hidden directly in the physical metric equations. It uses no packet choice and preserves the full one-third squarefree threshold.


The key observation is that the products
  eR, xy, UV
form a single integral Pythagorean triple. Its exact content is precisely the current physical gcd
  G_*=gcd(eR,xy).
The two diagonal bilinear gaps
  W_-:=UV-eR,
  W_+:=UV+eR
are then the Euclid gap factors of that macro triple and each separately carries the entire odd squarefree support of G_*.


2. Macro-Pythagorean identity


Retain the physical equations
  U^2=e^2+x^2,
  V^2=e^2+y^2,
  R^2=e^2+x^2+y^2.                               (229AR.1)


Then
  U^2 V^2
   =(e^2+x^2)(e^2+y^2)
   =e^4+e^2(x^2+y^2)+x^2y^2
   =e^2 R^2+x^2y^2.


Therefore
  (eR)^2+(xy)^2=(UV)^2.                          (229AR.2)


Thus
  (eR,xy,UV)
is a positive integral Pythagorean triple.


RESULT_229AR_MACRO_PYTHAGOREAN_TRIPLE=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Its exact content is the current G_*


Define
  G_*:=gcd(eR,xy),
as in the current quotient-free receiver.


In any integral Pythagorean triple A^2+B^2=C^2, the three pairwise gcds coincide with the content:
if p^k divides A and C, then p^(2k) divides C^2-A^2=B^2, hence p^k divides B; and similarly for the other pairs.


Applying this to (229AR.2),
  gcd(eR,xy)
   =gcd(eR,UV)
   =gcd(xy,UV)
   =gcd(eR,xy,UV).                               (229AR.3)


Hence
  G_*
   =content(eR,xy,UV)
   =gcd(eR,UV).                                   (229AR.4)


RESULT_229AR_GSTAR_IS_MACRO_TRIPLE_CONTENT=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AR_GSTAR_EQUALS_GCD_eR_UV=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AR_GSTAR_EQUALS_GCD_xy_UV=PROVED_EXACT.


This is a new diagonal-product form of the current physical gcd receiver:
  K_*=sf(G_*)=sf(gcd(eR,UV)).                     (229AR.5)


No quotient, selector substitution, or population change is involved.


4. Macro Euclid-root compression


Normalize the macro triple by its exact content:
  E0:=eR/G_*,
  X0:=xy/G_*,
  H0:=UV/G_*.
Then
  E0^2+X0^2=H0^2
is primitive.


Therefore there are coprime integers m>n>0 of opposite parity. There are two cases.


Case I: E0 is the even leg.
Then
  E0=2mn,
  X0=m^2-n^2,
  H0=m^2+n^2.
Thus
  H0-E0=(m-n)^2,
  H0+E0=(m+n)^2.


Case II: E0 is the odd leg.
Then
  E0=m^2-n^2,
  X0=2mn,
  H0=m^2+n^2.
Thus
  H0-E0=2n^2,
  H0+E0=2m^2.


Consequently there exist
  epsilon_macro in {0,1}
and coprime positive integers
  r_-<r_+
such that exactly
  UV-eR = 2^epsilon_macro G_* r_-^2,             (229AR.6)
  UV+eR = 2^epsilon_macro G_* r_+^2.             (229AR.7)


Moreover
  gcd(r_-,r_+)=1.                                (229AR.8)


In Case I one may take
  epsilon_macro=0,
  r_-=m-n,
  r_+=m+n.
Because m,n have opposite parity, r_-,r_+ are odd and coprime.


In Case II one may take
  epsilon_macro=1,
  r_-=n,
  r_+=m.


It follows immediately that
  gcd(UV-eR,UV+eR)
    =2^epsilon_macro G_*.                         (229AR.9)


Also, multiplying (229AR.6) and (229AR.7),
  (UV-eR)(UV+eR)
    =x^2y^2,                                      (229AR.10)
which recovers
  xy=2^epsilon_macro G_* r_- r_+.                (229AR.11)


RESULT_229AR_MACRO_GAPS_EQUAL_CONTENT_TIMES_COPRIME_SQUARES=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AR_MACRO_GAP_GCD_EQUALS_2EPS_GSTAR=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Positivity and exact single-scalar squarefree receiver


By (229AR.10), the product
  (UV-eR)(UV+eR)
is positive. Since UV+eR>0,
  UV-eR>0.                                        (229AR.12)


Thus the smaller bilinear gap
  W_-:=UV-eR
is a positive integer.


From (229AR.6),
  sf_odd(W_-)=sf_odd(G_*).                        (229AR.13)


Likewise from (229AR.7),
  sf_odd(W_+)=sf_odd(G_*),                        (229AR.14)
where
  W_+:=UV+eR.


Let
  K_odd:=sf_odd(G_*).
Then exactly
  K_odd
   =sf_odd(UV-eR)
   =sf_odd(UV+eR).                                (229AR.15)


RESULT_229AR_SINGLE_BILINEAR_GAP_CARRIES_FULL_ODD_KSTAR=PROVED_EXACT.

records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AQ — four-short-gap squarefree-kernel collapse and central-gap divisor chart


STATUS: POST_229AP_SHORT_GAP_SQUAREFREE_COLLAPSE_COMPLETE / PROVED_FOUR_PHYSICAL_GAPS_CARRY_EXACT_ODD_CONTENT_SQUAREFREE_KERNELS / PROVED_CANONICAL_TWIST_EQUALS_SF_OF_FOUR_SHORT_GAP_PRODUCT / PROVED_POSITIVE_CENTRAL_GAP / PROVED_CENTRAL_GAP_HYPERBOLA_IDENTITIES / PROVED_TWO_LINEAR_HEIGHT_O_B_TWIST_RECEIVER / PROVED_TWO_PACKET_ONE_SIXTH_THRESHOLD / PROVED_SMALL_OUTER_GAP_PRODUCT_SECTOR_H_ONE_PLUS_O1 / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AP EXACT SQUAREFREE-KERNEL RECEIVER / POSITIVE SHORT-GAP CHART / DIVISOR-FIBER COUNT / TWO-LINEAR-PACKET THRESHOLD IMPROVEMENT / METHOD FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AP
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1wnFmDhoEr4J0chnZFbVv0b_cMfcb6FwVhsGUw-HlID4


1. Scope


229AP upgraded the edge-content packetization from odd inert primes to every odd prime in a,b, but its preferred edge receiver used radicals and still left c12,c21 as a separate residual split-support pair.


The current whole-population gate, however, is a squarefree-kernel gate:
  K_* = sf(gcd(eR,xy))
      = sf(a b c12 c21).


229M already supplied the elementary Pythagorean content-squareclass lemma and the four positive gap factors
  U-e, V-e, R-U, R-V.
This card pushes that retained lemma one step further at the exact integer level, then uses the physical metric identities to compress the four gaps to a positive central-gap divisor chart.


The result is:
- the odd squarefree part of the entire K_* support is exactly carried by the four positive short gaps;
- the canonical moving twist itself is exactly the squarefree kernel of their product;
- the same product is square-equivalent to a product of only two O(B)-height linear physical forms;
- after removing their common odd gcd, this gives a two-packet squarefree receiver with threshold T^(1/2), hence B^(1/6-delta/2) at the current one-third gate;
- the sector with small outer-gap product (R-U)(R-V) has an unconditional H^(1+o(1)) same-physical count.


No full large-tail estimate follows yet.


Notation:
sf(n) denotes the positive squarefree representative of n in Q*/Q*2.
sf_odd(n) denotes its odd part.


2. Four positive short gaps carry the four content squarefree kernels exactly


Set
  A := U-e,
  B := V-e,
  C := R-U,
  D := R-V.                                      (229AQ.1)


All four are positive because
  e<U<R,
  e<V<R.


Retain the four physical Pythagorean triples and their contents:
  (e,x,U) has content b,
  (e,y,V) has content a,
  (U,y,R) has content c12,
  (V,x,R) has content c21.


Retain Lemma 229M.2:
if a positive integral Pythagorean triple
  X^2+Y^2=Z^2
has content c and X is the selected leg, then
  Z-X = c s^2
or
  Z-X = 2 c s^2
for some positive integer s, according to the primitive-leg parity.


Applying it to the four triples gives positive integers
  s_b,s_a,s_12,s_21
and bits
  rho_b,rho_a,rho_12,rho_21 in {0,1}
such that
  A = 2^rho_b  b   s_b^2,
  B = 2^rho_a  a   s_a^2,
  C = 2^rho_12 c12 s_12^2,
  D = 2^rho_21 c21 s_21^2.                       (229AQ.2)


Therefore, exactly,
  sf_odd(A)=sf_odd(b),
  sf_odd(B)=sf_odd(a),
  sf_odd(C)=sf_odd(c12),
  sf_odd(D)=sf_odd(c21).                          (229AQ.3)


Because a,b,c12,c21 are pairwise coprime by 229M, the four odd squarefree gap kernels in (229AQ.3) are pairwise coprime.


RESULT_229AQ_FOUR_SHORT_GAPS_EXACT_ODD_CONTENT_SQUAREFREE_KERNELS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AQ_FOUR_SHORT_GAP_ODD_KERNELS_PAIRWISE_COPRIME=PROVED_EXACT.


This is stronger for the current K_* gate than replacing squarefree kernels by radicals: square factors in a,b,c12,c21 are removed exactly rather than overcounted.


3. Exact four-gap representation of K_* and the canonical twist


Let
  S_gap := A B C D
         = (U-e)(V-e)(R-U)(R-V).                 (229AQ.4)


Multiplying (229AQ.2),
  S_gap
   = 2^rho a b c12 c21 * square,
where
  rho = rho_b+rho_a+rho_12+rho_21.


Hence the odd part of the current quotient-free support invariant is exactly
  K_odd
   := odd part of K_*
    = sf_odd(a b c12 c21)
    = sf_odd(S_gap).                              (229AQ.5)


By 229M, the canonical positive squarefree moving twist is the positive squarefree representative of the same rational squareclass as S_gap. Therefore exactly
  d_tw = sf(S_gap).                               (229AQ.6)


Equivalently, K_* and d_tw differ, if at all, only in their 2-adic bit, while their odd parts are identical.


RESULT_229AQ_KSTAR_ODD_EQUALS_FOUR_SHORT_GAP_KERNEL=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AQ_CANONICAL_TWIST_EQUALS_SF_FOUR_SHORT_GAP_PRODUCT=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Positive central gap


Define the new central short-gap difference
  lambda := U+V-R-e.                              (229AQ.7)


This lambda is positive.


Indeed,
  A = U-e = x^2/(U+e),
  D = R-V = x^2/(R+V).
Since R>U and V>e,
  R+V > U+e,
so
  A>D.
Thus
  lambda=A-D>0.


Similarly,
  B = y^2/(V+e),
  C = y^2/(R+U),
and R+U>V+e, so B>C and
  lambda=B-C.


Therefore
  A=D+lambda,
  B=C+lambda.                                    (229AQ.8)


Also
  0<lambda<A<R-e,
so
  lambda<R-e.                                    (229AQ.9)


RESULT_229AQ_CENTRAL_GAP_POSITIVE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AQ_GAP_PAIR_TRANSLATION=A_MINUS_D_EQ_B_MINUS_C_EQ_LAMBDA.


5. Central-gap hyperbola identities


Use
  x^2=A(U+e)=D(R+V).
Substitute A=D+lambda and
  R+V-(U+e)=2C+lambda.
Then
  (D+lambda)(U+e)=D[(U+e)+(2C+lambda)].
After cancellation,
  lambda(U+e)=D(2C+lambda).


Since U=e+D+lambda, this becomes
  lambda(2e+D+lambda)=2CD+D lambda,
hence
  lambda(2e+lambda)=2 C D.                       (229AQ.10)


The y-side gives the same identity.


Using A=D+lambda and B=C+lambda,
  A B
   = (D+lambda)(C+lambda)
   = C D + lambda(C+D)+lambda^2.
Combine with (229AQ.10) and
  R=e+C+D+lambda
to obtain
  lambda(2R+lambda)=2 A B.                       (229AQ.11)


Thus the two short-gap products satisfy the exact paired hyperbola system
  2(R-U)(R-V)
    = lambda(e+U+V-R),                            (229AQ.12)
  2(U-e)(V-e)
    = lambda(R+U+V-e).                            (229AQ.13)


Here
  2e+lambda = e+U+V-R,
  2R+lambda = R+U+V-e.


RESULT_229AQ_CENTRAL_GAP_HYPERBOLA_IDENTITIES=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Two O(B)-height linear forms carry the entire moving twist


Define
  L_- := 2e+lambda = e+U+V-R,
  L_+ := 2R+lambda = R+U+V-e.                    (229AQ.14)


By positivity of lambda,
  0<L_-<L_+.


Multiply (229AQ.10) and (229AQ.11):
  4 A B C D
    = lambda^2 L_- L_+.                          (229AQ.15)


Both 4 and lambda^2 are perfect squares. Hence
  [S_gap]=[L_- L_+]
in Q*/Q*2, and using (229AQ.6),
  d_tw = sf(L_- L_+).                            (229AQ.16)


For the current quotient-free support invariant,
  K_odd = sf_odd(L_- L_+).                       (229AQ.17)


The two forms have exact physical height O(B):
from lambda<R-e,
  L_- =2e+lambda < e+R <2B,
  L_+ =2R+lambda <3R-e <3B.                     (229AQ.18)


RESULT_229AQ_TWO_LINEAR_HEIGHT_O_B_TWIST_RECEIVER=PROVED_EXACT.


This removes both the four-gap product and the separate edge/split squarefree-support bookkeeping at the level of the canonical twist class. It does not remove the physical selector equations.


7. Exact two-packet odd squarefree receiver and improved threshold


Let
  g_L := gcd_odd(L_-,L_+),
and define
  ell_- := L_-/g_L,
  ell_+ := L_+/g_L.                              (229AQ.19)


Then
  gcd_odd(ell_-,ell_+)=1,
and
  L_-L_+ = g_L^2 ell_- ell_+.
Since g_L^2 is a square,
  K_odd
   = sf_odd(ell_- ell_+)
   = sf_odd(ell_-) sf_odd(ell_+),                (229AQ.20)
with the two displayed squarefree factors odd-coprime.


Therefore, for every T>=1,
  K_*>T
implies
  K_odd>T/2,
and hence
  max(sf_odd(ell_-), sf_odd(ell_+))
    > (T/2)^(1/2).                               (229AQ.21)


At the current gate
  T=B^(1/3-delta),
one of the two packets satisfies
  sf_odd(ell_±)
    > 2^(-1/2) B^(1/6-delta/2).                 (229AQ.22)


RESULT_229AQ_TWO_ODD_COPRIME_LINEAR_PACKETS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AQ_CURRENT_ONE_THIRD_GATE_TWO_PACKET_THRESHOLD=B_TO_ONE_SIXTH_MINUS_DELTA_OVER_TWO.


This is a theorem-interface improvement over the four-packet T^(1/4) edge receiver when the target is the full squarefree K_* support. The 229AP receiver remains useful because it retains finer edge-prime sign and height information.


No count for the large ell_- or ell_+ squarefree-kernel tails is proved here.


8. Divisor chart and a genuine scoped same-physical count


Equation (229AQ.10) gives
  lambda | 2 C D.                                (229AQ.23)


Moreover, given positive integers C,D,lambda from a physical endpoint,
  e = (2CD/lambda-lambda)/2,                     (229AQ.24)
and then uniquely
  U=e+D+lambda,
  V=e+C+lambda,
  R=e+C+D+lambda.                                (229AQ.25)


Once e,U,V,R are fixed, positive x,y,z, if they exist, are uniquely determined by
  x^2=U^2-e^2,
  y^2=V^2-e^2,
  z^2=R^2-e^2.
Thus the map from physical endpoints to labelled triples
  (C,D,lambda)
is injective.


Let
  N_out(H;B)
   := #{positive primitive physical endpoints R<=B :
         (R-U)(R-V)<=H}.


For each fixed C,D with CD<=H, lambda is a positive divisor of 2CD. Therefore
  N_out(H;B)
   <= sum_{C D<=H} tau(2CD)
   = H^(1+o(1)),                                 (229AQ.26)
uniformly in B.


Equivalently, for every fixed eta>0,
  N_out(B^(1/3-eta);B)
    = B^(1/3-eta+o(1))
    = o(B^(1/3)).                                (229AQ.27)


RESULT_229AQ_SMALL_OUTER_GAP_PRODUCT_COUNT=PROVED_SCOPED_o_M3_SCALE.


Because A>D and B>C,
  A B > C D.
Hence the small inner-gap-product sector AB<=H is contained in the already-counted CD<=H sector.


The current large-K_* gate may therefore, at an o(B^(1/3)) cost, be restricted for any fixed eta>0 to
  (R-U)(R-V) > B^(1/3-eta).                      (229AQ.28)


RESULT_229AQ_HARD_TAIL_OUTER_GAP_PRODUCT_LOCALIZATION=PROVED_SCOPED.


This is a genuine same-physical counting deduction, but it is only a sector disposal. It does not imply a global count and does not change GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.

CURRENT_PREFERRED_GATE remains:
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R<=B :
      sf(gcd(eR,xy)) > B^(1/3-delta)}
    = o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.

  229AQ two O(B)-height linear forms
    L_-=e+U+V-R,
    L_+=R+U+V-e,
  with
    K_odd=sf_odd(L_-L_+),
  normalized to two odd-coprime packets at threshold
    B^(1/6-delta/2).


CURRENT_PREFERRED_SHORT_GAP_EXACT_RECEIVER:
  d_tw=sf((U-e)(V-e)(R-U)(R-V))
      =sf(L_-L_+).


CURRENT_PREFERRED_EDGE_REFINEMENT:

SCOPED_DISPOSED_SECTOR:
  (R-U)(R-V)<=B^(1/3-eta)
for any fixed eta>0 contributes o(B^(1/3)).


HARD_REMAINDER may therefore be required to satisfy simultaneously
  sf(gcd(eR,xy))>B^(1/3-delta),
  (R-U)(R-V)>B^(1/3-eta),
plus the exact two-linear packet structure above.


NEXT_USEFUL_INPUT:
(A) same-physical squarefree-kernel tail estimate for one or both normalized linear packets ell_± at the B^(1/6-delta/2) threshold;
(B) exploit the central divisor chart lambda(2e+lambda)=2(R-U)(R-V) together with the remaining selector-square conditions;
(C) combine 229AP sign-resolved edge divisibility with the 229AQ two-linear whole-K_* packets;
(D) direct realized d_tw support count using d_tw=sf(L_-L_+).


10. Firewalls and unchanged global state


Do not:
- replace squarefree kernel by radical when invoking the new two-packet threshold;
- infer independence of L_- and L_+;
- infer a large-tail count from the O(B) height alone;
- promote the scoped CD-small estimate to the complementary CD-large sector;
- treat the central divisor relation as sufficient for the face/sphere square selectors;

records.title: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AP — full-odd edge-content gap-gcd square matrix and four-packet extension
records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AP — full-odd edge-content gap-gcd square matrix and four-packet extension


STATUS: POST_229AO_FULL_ODD_EDGE_PACKETIZATION_COMPLETE / PROVED_GCD_eV_EQUALS_a / PROVED_GCD_eU_EQUALS_b / PROVED_EXACT_FULL_ODD_GAP_GCD_SQUARE_MATRIX / PROVED_229AK_INERT_PACKETIZATION_IS_SPECIALIZATION / PROVED_FULL_ODD_AB_FOUR_PACKET_RECEIVER / PROVED_229AO_CUBIC_SHORT_GAP_CARRIER_EXTENDS_TO_FULL_ODD_a_b / SPLIT_SUPPORT_NARROWED_TO_c12_c21_OUTSIDE_EDGE_PACKETS / NO_COUNTING_PROMOTION / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AO SAME-PHYSICAL FULL-ODD EDGE SUPPORT / EXACT GAP-GCD SQUARE MATRIX / FOUR-PACKET THRESHOLD-PRESERVING EXTENSION / SPLIT-SUPPORT NARROWING / METHOD FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AO
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1ckNKRRU3UDiOT98tESsQ9skB_SNFZxvulruSfbpaCZw


1. Scope


229AJ packetized only the odd inert p≡3 mod4 part of the edge contents a,b. 229AK then refined those inert packets by face/space signs, while 229AO extracted deterministic gap-size information without paying the eight-packet threshold loss.


The same sign geometry is in fact exact for every odd prime dividing a or b, not only inert primes. The missing input is the exact pairwise-content structure from 229D.


This card proves an all-odd gap-gcd square matrix for the edge contents a=gcd(e,y) and b=gcd(e,x). Its p≡3 mod4 restriction is exactly the retained 229AK packetization. Aggregating by the space-gap sign gives a four-packet receiver for rad_odd(ab), including split primes carried by a,b, and extends the 229AO cubic short-gap carrier from a_(3),b_(3) to the complete odd parts a_odd,b_odd.


This is a structural extension only. It does not count the packets and does not control the separate split-only contents c12,c21.


2. Retained exact physical factorization


Retain 229D/229M:
  e = g a b,
  x = d0 b c,
  y = d0 a f,
with
  gcd(a,b)=1,
  gcd(e,x)=b,
  gcd(e,y)=a,
and primitive face triples
  T_a=(g a,d0 c,n1),
  T_b=(g b,d0 f,n2).


Retain
  U=b n1,
  V=a n2.


Because T_a and T_b are primitive,
  gcd(g a,n1)=1,
  gcd(g b,n2)=1.
Therefore
  gcd(e,U)=b*gcd(g a,n1)=b,                    (229AP.1)
  gcd(e,V)=a*gcd(g b,n2)=a.                    (229AP.2)


RESULT_229AP_GCD_eU_EQUALS_b=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AP_GCD_eV_EQUALS_a=PROVED_EXACT.


These two identities are the full-odd analogue of the inert-support localization used implicitly in 229AJ/229AK.


3. Exact full-odd a-side gap-gcd square matrix


For positive integers A,B write gcd_odd(A,B) for the largest odd divisor of gcd(A,B).


For sigma,tau in {-,+}, define alpha_{sigma,tau} by
  alpha_{sigma,tau}^2
    := gcd_odd(U+sigma x, R+tau x).              (229AP.3)


We prove that the right side is always a perfect square and that the four alpha packets partition a_odd exactly.


First let an odd prime p divide both U+sigma x and R+tau x. Then
  p | U^2-x^2 = e^2,
  p | R^2-x^2 = V^2.
Hence p|e and p|V, so by (229AP.2),
  p | gcd(e,V)=a.                                (229AP.4)


Conversely fix p^k || a, p odd. Since p|e and gcd(e,x)=b with gcd(a,b)=1,
  p does not divide x.
Then U^2=e^2+x^2 and R^2=V^2+x^2 show p does not divide U or R.


Thus exactly one of U-x,U+x is divisible by p, and exactly one of R-x,R+x is divisible by p. Let their signs be sigma(p),tau(p). Since the opposite factors are p-units,
  v_p(U+sigma(p)x)=v_p(e^2)=2v_p(e),
  v_p(R+tau(p)x)=v_p(V^2)=2v_p(V).


Using gcd(e,V)=a,
  min(v_p(e),v_p(V))=v_p(a)=k.
Therefore
  v_p(gcd_odd(U+sigma(p)x,R+tau(p)x))=2k.         (229AP.5)


For the other three sign pairs the p-adic valuation is zero.


Consequently every gcd in (229AP.3) is a square and
  a_odd = product_{sigma,tau} alpha_{sigma,tau}, (229AP.6)
with the four alpha_{sigma,tau} pairwise coprime.


RESULT_229AP_A_FULL_ODD_GAP_GCD_SQUARE_MATRIX=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Exact full-odd b-side gap-gcd square matrix


Define beta_{sigma,tau} by
  beta_{sigma,tau}^2
    := gcd_odd(V+sigma y, R+tau y).               (229AP.7)


The same argument uses
  V^2-y^2=e^2,
  R^2-y^2=U^2,
  gcd(e,U)=b,
  gcd(e,y)=a,
  gcd(a,b)=1.


For every odd p^k||b there is a unique sign pair (sigma(p),tau(p)) and
  v_p(gcd_odd(V+sigma(p)y,R+tau(p)y))=2k.
Hence
  b_odd = product_{sigma,tau} beta_{sigma,tau},  (229AP.8)
and the four beta packets are pairwise coprime.


Since gcd(a,b)=1, all eight alpha/beta packets are pairwise coprime.


RESULT_229AP_B_FULL_ODD_GAP_GCD_SQUARE_MATRIX=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AP_EIGHT_FULL_ODD_EDGE_PACKETS_PAIRWISE_COPRIME=PROVED_EXACT.


5. 229AK is exactly the inert specialization


For p≡3 mod4, the sign allocation in Sections 3–4 is the same unique allocation used in 229AK:
- the face-space sign is determined by which face gap contains p^k;
- the space sign is determined by which R±x or R±y gap contains p^k.


Therefore the p≡3 mod4 part of alpha_{sigma,tau} is exactly the retained 229AK packet a_{sigma,tau}, and the p≡3 mod4 part of beta_{sigma,tau} is exactly b_{sigma,tau}.


RESULT_229AP_229AK_INERT_PACKETS_ARE_FULL_ODD_PACKET_SPECIALIZATION=PROVED_EXACT.


No 229AK statement is retracted. 229AP enlarges its support from inert edge primes to every odd edge-content prime.


6. Four aggregated full-odd edge packets


Aggregate by the space-gap sign:
  alpha_tau = alpha_{-,tau} alpha_{+,tau},
  beta_tau  = beta_{-,tau} beta_{+,tau}.          (229AP.9)


Then
  a_odd = alpha_- alpha_+,
  b_odd = beta_- beta_+,                          (229AP.10)
and alpha_-,alpha_+,beta_-,beta_+ are pairwise coprime.


There are also exact aggregated gcd identities:
  alpha_tau^2 = gcd_odd(e^2,R+tau x),             (229AP.11)
  beta_tau^2  = gcd_odd(e^2,R+tau y).             (229AP.12)


Proof of (229AP.11): any odd common prime of e and R+tau x also divides
  R^2-x^2=V^2,
so it lies in gcd(e,V)=a. The p-adic valuation is
  2 min(v_p(e),v_p(V)) = 2v_p(a),
and the unique tau sign partitions the odd primes of a. The b-side is identical using gcd(e,U)=b.


Set
  Abar_tau=rad(alpha_tau),
  Bbar_tau=rad(beta_tau).
Then
  rad_odd(ab)
    = Abar_- Abar_+ Bbar_- Bbar_+.                (229AP.13)


Hence for every T>=1,
  rad_odd(ab)>T
    =>
  max(Abar_-,Abar_+,Bbar_-,Bbar_+)>T^(1/4).       (229AP.14)


RESULT_229AP_FULL_ODD_AB_FOUR_PACKET_RECEIVER=PROVED_EXACT.


At a threshold T=B^(1/3-delta), the corresponding packet threshold is again
  B^(1/12-delta/4).
This is the same quarter-threshold as 229AJ, now for all odd primes in a,b rather than only inert primes.


No endpoint count is asserted.


7. Full-odd extension of the 229AO short-gap carrier


From the definitions,
  alpha_-^2 | R-x,
  beta_-^2  | R-y.                                (229AP.15)


For the plus aggregates, alpha_{-,+}^2 divides U-x and alpha_{+,+}^2 divides both U+x and R+x. Their difference gives
  alpha_{+,+}^2 | R-U.
Since alpha_{-,+} and alpha_{+,+} are coprime,
  alpha_+^2 | (U-x)(R-U).                         (229AP.16)


Similarly
  beta_+^2 | (V-y)(R-V).                          (229AP.17)


Using a_odd=alpha_-alpha_+ and b_odd=beta_-beta_+,
  a_odd^2 | (R-x)(U-x)(R-U),                     (229AP.18)
  b_odd^2 | (R-y)(V-y)(R-V).                     (229AP.19)


Retain positivity x<U<R and y<V<R from 229AO. Since
  (U-x)+(R-U)=R-x,
  (V-y)+(R-V)=R-y,
AM-GM yields
  4 a_odd^2 <= (R-x)^3,                           (229AP.20)
  4 b_odd^2 <= (R-y)^3.                           (229AP.21)


In particular, for every M>0,
  Abar_->M => R-x>M^2,
  Abar_+>M => R-x>2M,
  Bbar_->M => R-y>M^2,
  Bbar_+>M => R-y>2M.                             (229AP.22)


RESULT_229AP_229AO_CUBIC_SHORT_GAP_CARRIER_EXTENDS_TO_FULL_ODD_EDGE_CONTENT=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AP_FULL_ODD_FOUR_PACKET_HEIGHT_LOCALIZATION=PROVED_EXACT.


8. Split-support consequence


Retain 229M:
  K_* = sf(a b c12 c21),
and a,b,c12,c21 are pairwise coprime.


Retain 229AI:
- every odd prime of c12 or c21 is split, p≡1 mod4;
- the inert part of K_* lies entirely in a,b.


229AP now adds that every odd prime in a,b, including split primes, is captured by the four aggregated edge packets (229AP.9).


Therefore, outside the 2-adic bit, the only K_* support not represented by the full-odd edge four-packet receiver is the pair of split-only physical contents
  c12, c21.                                       (229AP.23)


RESULT_229AP_SPLIT_SUPPORT_OUTSIDE_EDGE_PACKETS_LOCALIZED_TO_c12_c21=PROVED_EXACT.


This is a structural narrowing only. It does not show that c12 or c21 is small, sparse, or negligible, and it does not convert the whole K_* tail to the edge four-packet tail.


The raw-content large-tail problem of 229M also remains distinct: a large a or b can arise from repeated prime powers while rad_odd(ab) is smaller. No 229M raw-size gate is declared closed.


9. Quantitative firewall and next theorem interface


What 229AP improves:
- 229AJ/229AK inert packetization is upgraded to all odd edge-content primes;
- the same T^(1/4) four-packet threshold is preserved for rad_odd(ab);
- 229AO height localization and cubic short-gap carriers now hold for the complete odd edge contents;
- split support is separated into split edge primes already inside the new packets versus the residual split-only contents c12,c21.


What 229AP does NOT prove:
- no same-physical packet counting estimate;
- no polynomial saving;
- no independence between gap divisibilities;
- no large-c12/c21 tail estimate;
- no closure of the full sf(gcd(eR,xy)) one-third gate;
- no counting promotion.


CURRENT_PREFERRED_GATE remains:
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R<=B :
      sf(gcd(eR,xy)) > B^(1/3-delta)}
    = o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


CURRENT_PREFERRED_EDGE_CONTENT_STRUCTURAL_RECEIVER:
  229AP full-odd four packets for rad_odd(ab), threshold T^(1/4), with 229AP height localization.


CURRENT_PREFERRED_INERT_STRUCTURAL_RECEIVER remains:
  229AJ four inert packets, now identified as the p≡3 mod4 specialization of 229AP.


NEXT_USEFUL_INPUT:
(A) same-physical count for the 229AP full-odd four edge packets exploiting exact R-height and gap localization;
(B) a genuine count/tail theorem for the residual split-only c12,c21 contents, preferably coupled to the 229AP edge packets;
(C) direct realized K_* or moving-twist support counting;
(D) cross-prime cancellation/dispersion across edge packets and c12,c21.


Do not infer density from the exact gcd-square identities themselves. Do not multiply sign incidences as independent. Do not identify raw content size with squarefree radical size.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.

INTEGRATED_AUDIT_186_229O_SCOPE=UNCHANGED_NOT_EXTENDED_TO_229P_THROUGH_229AP.


10. Dependencies and verification scope


Internal load-bearing inputs:
- 229D exact physical factorization and pairwise contents;
- 229M four physical contents and pairwise coprimality;
- 229AJ inert four-packet receiver;
- 229AK sign-resolved inert face/space packets;

A targeted literature rematch found general toric bounded-height, rational-point sieve, and recent thin-set counting results, but no theorem was identified that directly supplies the required same-physical 229AP packet count with exact R-height. This is not an absence theorem and no literature-based no-go is claimed.

records.title: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AO — threshold-preserving short-gap height coupling for the 229AJ four-packet receiver
records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AO — threshold-preserving short-gap height coupling for the 229AJ four-packet receiver


STATUS: POST_229AN_FOUR_PACKET_SHORT_GAP_HEIGHT_COUPLING_COMPLETE / PROVED_A_PLUS_SQUARE_DIVIDES_TWO_SHORT_GAPS / PROVED_B_PLUS_SQUARE_DIVIDES_TWO_SHORT_GAPS / PROVED_CUBIC_SHORT_GAP_CARRIER_FOR_FULL_INERT_a_b_CONTENT / FOUR_PACKET_THRESHOLD_PRESERVED / NO_COUNTING_PROMOTION / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229AN SAME-PHYSICAL HEIGHT COUPLING / FOUR-PACKET THRESHOLD-PRESERVING SIZE ADAPTER / POSITIVE-GAP PRODUCT IDENTITY / METHOD FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229AN
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0
CARD_DOC_ID: 1dkSwIKkZ0AEyiHQl_SsyMTF-X2FrWX7qvTP6CBnLgTs


1. Scope


229AN proves that the threshold-preserving 229AL common-root gcd events are pointwise identical to the original 229AJ four-packet events, so 229AL itself supplies no extra local incidence or gcd-density saving. The remaining useful internal direction is therefore quantitative information beyond event identity: packet size, physical height, or global distribution.


This card extracts such information from the retained 229AK/229AM sign-resolved gap cycle without paying the 229AK eight-packet threshold loss.


The key observation is that positivity gives two strict chains
  x < U < R,
  y < V < R,
because U^2=e^2+x^2, V^2=e^2+y^2, and R^2=U^2+y^2=V^2+x^2.


The 229AK intersection packets already know which face/space signs occur, and 229AM gives the forced third sign. Aggregating those sign data in the correct way yields exact divisibility of the 229AJ plus-packets by products of the two positive short subgaps U-x and R-U, or V-y and R-V.


No external theorem is used. No endpoint saving is claimed.


2. Retained packet notation and three-gap sign law


Retain 229AJ/229AK/229AM.


For sigma,tau in {-,+}, let a_{sigma,tau}, b_{sigma,tau} be the eight pairwise-coprime inert intersection packets. Let
  a_tau = product_sigma a_{sigma,tau},
  b_tau = product_sigma b_{sigma,tau},
so
  a_(3)=a_- a_+,
  b_(3)=b_- b_+,
with gcd(a_-,a_+)=gcd(b_-,b_+)=1.


Their radicals are
  A_tau=rad(a_tau),
  B_tau=rad(b_tau),
and
  rad_3(K_*)=A_- A_+ B_- B_+.


For m=a_{sigma,tau}, 229AK/229AM give
  m^2 | U + sigma x,
  m^2 | R + tau x,
  m^2 | R - tau sigma U.                         (229AO.1)


For m=b_{sigma,tau},
  m^2 | V + sigma y,
  m^2 | R + tau y,
  m^2 | R - tau sigma V.                         (229AO.2)


The third congruence is dependent and is not assigned an independent density. Here it is used only for deterministic size coupling.


3. Threshold-preserving plus-packet short-gap product


Consider the a-side plus packet a_+=a_{-,+}a_{+,+}.


For m=a_{-,+}, sigma=- and tau=+, so (229AO.1) gives
  m^2 | U-x.


For m=a_{+,+}, sigma=+ and tau=+, so the forced third gap in (229AO.1) is
  m^2 | R-U.


Because a_{-,+} and a_{+,+} are coprime,
  a_+^2 | (U-x)(R-U).                             (229AO.3)


Likewise, on the b side,
  b_+^2 | (V-y)(R-V).                             (229AO.4)


RESULT_229AO_A_PLUS_TWO_SHORT_GAP_PRODUCT=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AO_B_PLUS_TWO_SHORT_GAP_PRODUCT=PROVED_EXACT.


This is genuinely more than the 229AN event-equivalent 229AL representation: it records actual positive magnitudes of two subgaps on the same physical endpoint. It does not split A_+ or B_+ into two threshold events.


4. Cubic short-gap carrier for the full inert a/b contents


229AJ already gives
  a_-^2 | R-x,
  b_-^2 | R-y.                                    (229AO.5)


Combining (229AO.3)-(229AO.5) with coprimality of the plus/minus packets gives
  a_(3)^2 | (R-x)(U-x)(R-U),                      (229AO.6)
  b_(3)^2 | (R-y)(V-y)(R-V).                      (229AO.7)


Now set
  D_x=R-x=(U-x)+(R-U),
  D_y=R-y=(V-y)+(R-V).
All summands are positive. By AM-GM,
  (U-x)(R-U) <= D_x^2/4,
  (V-y)(R-V) <= D_y^2/4.


Therefore
  4 a_(3)^2 <= (R-x)^3,                           (229AO.8)
  4 b_(3)^2 <= (R-y)^3.                           (229AO.9)


Equivalently,
  a_(3) <= (R-x)^(3/2)/2,
  b_(3) <= (R-y)^(3/2)/2.                         (229AO.10)


Since rad_3(a)<=a_(3) and rad_3(b)<=b_(3), the same upper envelopes hold for the inert radicals of a and b.


RESULT_229AO_FULL_INERT_a_CUBIC_SHORT_GAP_CARRIER=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229AO_FULL_INERT_b_CUBIC_SHORT_GAP_CARRIER=PROVED_EXACT.


5. Four-packet height localization without the eight-packet threshold loss


From (229AO.3)-(229AO.5),
  a_- <= sqrt(R-x),
  a_+ <= (R-x)/2,
  b_- <= sqrt(R-y),
  b_+ <= (R-y)/2.                                 (229AO.11)


Hence, for every M>0,
  A_->M  =>  R-x > M^2,
  A_+>M  =>  R-x > 2M,
  B_->M  =>  R-y > M^2,
  B_+>M  =>  R-y > 2M.                            (229AO.12)


These are exact necessary physical-height conditions attached directly to the existing 229AJ four packet events. No T^(1/8) subdivision is required.


At the current 229AJ receiver threshold
  M=B^(1/12-delta/4),
the minus-packet events lie only in
  R-x > B^(1/6-delta/2) or R-y > B^(1/6-delta/2),
while the plus-packet events lie only in
  R-x > 2 B^(1/12-delta/4) or R-y > 2 B^(1/12-delta/4).   (229AO.13)


This is a height-localization adapter, not a saving theorem. Large lower gaps may still occur on a large portion of the physical locus.


RESULT_229AO_FOUR_PACKET_THRESHOLD_PRESERVED_WITH_HEIGHT_COUPLING=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Quantitative interpretation and firewall


229AO sharpens the theorem interface in a way allowed by the 229AN firewall.


What is new:
- the four preferred 229AJ packet events now carry deterministic same-physical gap-size constraints;
- the plus packets are controlled by products of the two short positive subgaps of x<U<R and y<V<R;
- the full inert a/b contents satisfy the cubic short-gap carrier (229AO.8)-(229AO.9);
- all of this preserves the four-packet threshold B^(1/12-delta/4).


What is NOT proved:
- no endpoint count is improved;
- no local-density or independence factor is created;
- the two short subgaps in (229AO.3)-(229AO.4) must not be treated as independent random divisibility events;
- the lower bounds in (229AO.12)-(229AO.13) are not by themselves sparse-region statements;
- no split-side closure follows.


Do not multiply the 229AK/229AM congruence incidences. The only use of the sign cycle here is deterministic divisibility plus positivity/AM-GM.


7. Operational consequence


CURRENT_PREFERRED_GATE remains
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R<=B :
      sf(gcd(eR,xy)) > B^(1/3-delta)}
    = o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


CURRENT_PREFERRED_INERT_STRUCTURAL_RECEIVER remains 229AJ four realized Euclid-root packets at threshold B^(1/12-delta/4).


229AO adds:
  FOUR_PACKET_HEIGHT_COUPLING_REFINEMENT=ACTIVE_AS_STRUCTURAL_INTERFACE_ONLY.


The next genuinely useful quantitative input may be any of:
(A) a same-physical count for the 229AJ four packet events that exploits the automatic gap-size localization (229AO.12), for example a dyadic joint count in packet size and R-x/R-y;
(B) a theorem for the positive short-gap products (U-x)(R-U) or (V-y)(R-V) with the exact physical R-height and primitive masks;
(C) a direct support theorem for realized K_* or the moving twist classes;
(D) a joint inert/split support theorem with genuine polynomial saving;
(E) cross-prime cancellation/dispersion across a,b,c12,c21.


Do not reopen 229AL as an extra gcd-incidence filter. Do not promote 229AK eight-packet counting merely from the finer sign partition. Use 229AO only when a quantitative argument actually exploits the new size/height information.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_OPERATION=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.
PRIMARY_GATE=M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
INTEGRATED_AUDIT_186_229O_SCOPE=UNCHANGED_NOT_EXTENDED_TO_229P_THROUGH_229AO.


8. Dependencies and verification scope


Internal load-bearing inputs:
- 229AJ four clean space-root packets, pairwise coprimality, and the preferred T^(1/4) receiver;
- 229AK sign-resolved face/space intersection packets and double-gap divisibility;
